adjudication_records.issue_text: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:64 — detectProvider's selection semantics changed from fail-fast (IllegalStateException on multiple providers) to silently picking the highest-order provider and logging the rest only at debug level, removing a startup safeguard that deployments/tests may rely on to catch classpath misconfiguration, with no deprecation notice or migration guide

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` no longer throws when multiple `CryptoProvider`s are present. Instead it sorts by `CryptoProvider::order` descending and returns the first, while only logging the rest at `debug` (see removal of the `else if (foundProviders.size() > 1) { throw ... }` block and addition of sorting + "Ignored crypto providers" debug logging). This is a real behavioral/selection-semantics change that removes the previous fail-fast safeguard and could affect deployments/tests relying on the exception to detect classpath misconfiguration, but it is not inherently a correctness bug if the new ordering mechanism is intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:31 — Round-trip test only checks concat->DER->concat self-consistency with a self-generated signature; a symmetric bug present in both concatenatedRSToASN1DER and asn1derToConcatenatedRS (e.g. wrong leading-zero handling) would cancel out and still pass

adjudication.rationale: The new test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` only asserts `rsConcat` equals `rsConcat2` after doing `DER(signature) -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS -> concatenatedRSToASN1DER -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS` (see `test(...)`: `sign`, `rsConcat`, `asn1Des`, `rsConcat2`, `Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2)`). It never checks that `rsConcat` is the *correct* RS for the original JCA-produced DER signature, nor that `asn1Des` matches the original `sign` or successfully verifies. Therefore an error in `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` (and/or a complementary error in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, e.g., leading-zero/sign-bit handling) could still pass because the round-trip only tests internal consistency, not correctness against an external oracle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:70 — New order() method (returns 100, lower than DefaultCryptoProvider/WildFlyElytronProvider/FIPS1402Provider which all return 200) has no test verifying this value or its precedence relative to the other providers when multiple are present on the classpath

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new provider-selection behavior based on `CryptoProvider.order()` (see `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` now sorting providers by `order()` descending and no longer failing when multiple providers are present). `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` implements `order()` returning 100, while `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` return 200. There is a new unit test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) for signature conversion, but nothing in the diff tests provider precedence/selection when multiple `CryptoProvider` implementations are on the classpath, so the finding about missing test coverage for this nontrivial new selection logic is grounded.
